subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should the public cron run API permanently use non-consuming operator semantics for every caller, reserving consuming scheduler state exclusively for timer and gateway on-exit internals?
rationale: This fixes destructive behavior but intentionally changes observable behavior for existing CLI, RPC, and in-process facade callers; tests cannot decide whether that compatibility contract is the intended product policy.

options.title: Adopt operator-only public runs
options.body: Merge after current-head live proof, treating manual execution as diagnostic/verification behavior that records outcomes without consuming scheduler-owned state.

options.title: Preserve an explicit consuming public operation
options.body: Define and document a separate narrowly authorized public API if supported callers legitimately need to consume one-shots or scheduler state.

options.title: Pause for cron API design review
options.body: Hold the branch if maintainers want a broader public API contract discussion before changing established force-run behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt operator-only public runs
recommendation.body: Merge after current-head live proof, treating manual execution as diagnostic/verification behavior that records outcomes without consuming scheduler-owned state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the closely related due-slot and cron scheduling invariants implicated by this compatibility decision.
